page: OVHcloud d2-4 is an entry-level virtual instance belonging to the Discovery server family, virtualized on KVM. It features 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Intel Haswell architecture processor operating at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, supporting standard x86_64 instruction set extensions including AVX, AES, and FMA, but lacking newer vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX.

Memory capacity is configured at 4.0 GB total, delivering an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Attached local storage consists of a bundled 50 GB NVMe solid-state drive. The instance lacks dedicated hardware acceleration with zero GPUs and lists a 0 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile along with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included by default.

Empirical benchmark results place the compute and memory performance of the d2-4 in the bottom decile across tested cloud instances. It recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 519.0 and a multi-core score of 919.0, matched by a PassMark CPU score of 2054.9 and stress-ng throughput of 1818.26 in multi-core operations. Memory operations reached 19.19 GB/sec for uncached read bandwidth and 14.22 GB/sec for uncached write bandwidth. In application tests, Redis achieved 2.07 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 1.89 GB/sec.

Due to its shared legacy CPU architecture and constrained memory footprint, this instance is suited primarily for low-resource utility roles. These include lightweight testing environments, educational sandbox development, staging systems, and non-critical background automation that do not require high throughput, low latency, or guaranteed network capacity.
